svg.text: Tools: grep, glob, tree, search_notes and overview
tools.py: what the model calls to look through the user's files. Every result is text with source ids. working tree on 5ca550a, 2026-10-12.
the pattern checked with Python's re first
declared folders, and folders allowed this session,
or the folder a ~ or absolute pattern names
a folder named in the pattern is searched,
unless the user excluded it; a file once
Each file: how to read it?
a type parse does not read → skipped
text over 20 MiB → counted, not searched
current hash matches converted text → store
else valid UTF-8 → ripgrep, other text → converter
400 paths a call, every matching line
a NUL byte → the file dropped (binary)
a store line → its page, cell or line
what the index has not seen as it is;
everything when ripgrep is missing or refuses a
every match, whole: each file's first in walk order,
the whole result: the agent shows what fits
files the user may not read: counted
every candidate, best first: (before) the hit
not enough → what the index does not hold,
every entry; ≤ 4 levels (bounds the walk's time)
a folder grep would skip: named with its reason
(files.check), not opened; hidden, protected: not shown
the same walk; every file listed;
what was not listed, counted by reason
Searcher.documents: every file once, by its best
passage (whole, one line); headings, first line;
no query: the folder's catalog by path
13,402 files: ripgrep 2.2 s, converter only 6.1 s,
the same output (old Python grep: 43.8 s);
Docker: rg from pixi, none on the system;
working tree on 5ca550a, 2026-10-12; their state is kept in STATUS.md
grep walks the folders on every call (files.walk: 1.1–1.4 s of 2.2 s for 13,402 files on the owner's machine); speed on a large corpus and on macOS
pixi.toml lists linux-64 only: peresearch, and the ripgrep it ships, do not install on macOS or Windows yet
